title: Chapter 16 — The Brand Ladder & Tiering
intro: Tiers, brand identities, family trees, and how to answer the brand question honestly.

sections.title: The Four Tiers
sections.content:
Every appliance brand sits on a tier. Understanding where each brand lives — and why — is how you navigate the brand conversation with customers.

Entry tier: Amana, Hotpoint, Frigidaire base, Beko, Avanti. Reliable, affordable, no-frills. Perfect for rentals, first homes, basements, and budget-conscious buyers. Never apologize for recommending entry tier when it is the right fit.

Mid-range: Whirlpool, GE Appliances, Frigidaire Gallery, Samsung, LG, Maytag. The workhorses. Most of your floor volume lives here. These are the brands that balance features with value.

Premium: Bosch, KitchenAid, Electrolux, GE Profile, Frigidaire Professional, LG Studio, Fisher & Paykel. The step-up tier. Better materials, better engineering, better design. This is where the step-up conversation lives.

Luxury: Sub-Zero, Wolf, Cove, Miele, Thermador, Gaggenau, JennAir, Monogram, La Cornue, BlueStar. Design-driven, performance-driven, often custom or panel-ready. This is consultation selling, not transaction selling.

sections.title: The Brand Family Trees
sections.content:
Understanding who owns whom helps you navigate recommendations and compatibility.

Whirlpool Corporation owns Whirlpool, Maytag, KitchenAid, JennAir, Amana, and Gladiator. Their products share some engineering platforms but each brand has a distinct identity and market position.

BSH (Bosch Siemens Hausgerate) owns Bosch, Thermador, and Gaggenau. European engineering throughout. Bosch is premium. Thermador is luxury with the One-Two-Free program. Gaggenau is ultra-luxury.

Haier Group owns GE Appliances, Café, Monogram, Hotpoint, Fisher & Paykel, and Haier brand. GE Appliances is the broadest portfolio in North America — from Hotpoint at entry to Monogram at luxury.

Electrolux Group owns Electrolux and Frigidaire (base, Gallery, Professional). Two distinct brand identities on shared platforms.

Sub-Zero Group owns Sub-Zero, Wolf, and Cove. All manufactured in Madison, Wisconsin. This is the luxury trio that architects and designers specify most often.

sections.title: How to Answer the Brand Question
sections.content:
The customer asks: 'What brand should I buy?' This is not a brand question — it is a needs question wearing a brand disguise.

Never lead with brand. Lead with their needs. 'Let me understand what matters most to you, and then I will tell you which brands deliver on that.'

Once you understand their priorities — noise, reliability, design, budget, smart features, specific category needs — then the brand recommendation becomes obvious. 'You told me quiet operation and a third rack are your top priorities. At your budget, Bosch is the answer. If you want to step up for the zeolite drying system, the 800 series is worth the difference.'

When comparing brands, be honest about strengths and weaknesses. Every brand has both. The rep who admits a weakness — 'Samsung has great smart features but their service network is thinner than Bosch' — earns more trust than the rep who says 'Samsung is amazing at everything.'

Never trash a brand. If a customer came in wanting Brand X and you think Brand Y is better, show them both and let the product speak. Your job is to inform, not to campaign.
